name: Sunday Gravy and Pasta
base_description: Italian-American Sunday gravy (red sauce) with mixed meats, served over pasta with banana nut bread and fresh sandwich bread on the side
flavor_profile: Rich, savory, slow-cooked tomato depth with meaty umami and herbal brightness

elevations.title: Brown the Meats in Stages
elevations.instruction: Sear meats individually in a screaming-hot Dutch oven with canola oil. Get a hard, dark crust on each piece before removing. This fond is liquid gold. 3-4 minutes per side, undisturbed.
elevations.why: Maillard reaction creates hundreds of new flavor compounds. That fond becomes the backbone of your gravy.

elevations.title: Parmigiano Rind in the Gravy
elevations.instruction: Drop a 3-inch piece of Parmigiano-Reggiano rind into the gravy during the last 90 minutes. It softens, releases umami, and adds silky body.
elevations.why: The rind is concentrated glutamate. It adds savory depth and body without changing the flavor profile.

elevations.title: Fresh Basil and Good Olive Oil Finish
elevations.instruction: Tear 8-10 fresh basil leaves over plated pasta. Finish with a thread of your best extra-virgin olive oil.
elevations.why: Fresh basil on hot pasta releases volatile aromatics that cooked basil has lost. Raw olive oil provides fruity brightness.

elevations.title: Garlic Butter Toast
elevations.instruction: Mix softened butter with grated garlic, flaky salt, and minced parsley. Spread on thick bread slices and broil until golden (90 seconds max).
elevations.why: Real garlic bread with fresh garlic is a completely different animal. Broiler gives crackly top with butter-soaked interior.

designers_note: Sunday gravy is a labor of love. Brown meats properly, simmer low and slow for at least 3 hours, and resist stirring more than once every 30 minutes. The pot does the work.

name: Shepherds Pie
base_description: Classic British comfort with ground lamb or beef, peas, carrots under mashed potato crust, baked golden
flavor_profile: Savory, earthy, rich meat filling with creamy starchy topping

elevations.title: Bloom Your Tomato Paste
elevations.instruction: After browning meat, push aside and add 2 tbsp tomato paste to bare pan. Cook 2 full minutes until brick-red and sweet-smelling, then stir into meat.
elevations.why: Blooming caramelizes the sugars and concentrates umami - tastes like three times as much tomato.

elevations.title: Red Wine and Worcestershire
elevations.instruction: Pour half cup dry red wine and reduce by half. Add generous tablespoon of Worcestershire with the stock.
elevations.why: Wine brings tannin and acid that cut through richness. Worcestershire is fermented anchovy-tamarind magic.

elevations.title: Fork-Raked Top with Butter Dots
elevations.instruction: Drag fork across potato surface in crosshatch. Dot with small pieces of cold butter. Bake at 400F until ridges are deeply golden.
elevations.why: Ridges create browning surface area. Cold butter melts into peaks creating golden crispy spots contrasting creamy potato.

elevations.title: Fresh Thyme and Flaky Salt
elevations.instruction: Scatter fresh thyme leaves and Maldon salt over golden top right out of the oven.
elevations.why: Fresh herbs on hot surface release essential oils. Flaky salt adds crunch and controlled seasoning bursts.

designers_note: Snow day food at its finest. The filling must be thick, not soupy. Reduce until a spoon drawn through leaves a trail for 3 seconds. Wet filling makes soggy pie.

name: Babo Pasta
base_description: Homemade spinach pasta with only egg yolks - family favorite with rich, silky noodles
flavor_profile: Rich egg-yolk pasta with earthy spinach, silky texture

elevations.title: Rest Dough 45 Minutes
elevations.instruction: Rest wrapped dough for full 45 minutes at room temp. The extra time lets gluten relax completely for thinner, more even rolling.
elevations.why: Under-rested dough fights the roller. Fully relaxed dough rolls to translucent thinness and cooks to silky, melting texture.

elevations.title: Brown Butter with Crispy Sage
elevations.instruction: Melt 4 tbsp butter over medium heat. When foam subsides, add 12-15 sage leaves. Cook until butter is nutty-brown and sage crispy (60-90 sec). Kill heat. Toss pasta with splash of pasta water.
elevations.why: Brown butter milk solids caramelize creating nutty, toasty compounds that pair beautifully with egg-rich dough.

elevations.title: Toasted Pine Nuts and Microplaned Parm
elevations.instruction: Toast pine nuts in dry pan until golden (3-4 min, watch carefully). Scatter over pasta. Grate Parmigiano on Microplane so it falls like snow.
elevations.why: Pine nuts add buttery crunch against soft noodle. Microplaned cheese melts on contact creating umami veil.

elevations.title: Lemon Zest Shower
elevations.instruction: Zest half a lemon directly over each plate using Microplane just before serving.
elevations.why: Brown butter is rich. Lemon zest adds brightness without liquid, waking up every other flavor.

designers_note: When pasta is this good, sauce should honor it, not compete. Brown butter and sage is one of the oldest perfect pairings in Italian cooking. Keep it simple. Let the noodle be the star.

name: Niku Udon
base_description: Japanese meat udon - chewy noodles in savory-sweet broth with sliced beef and scallions
flavor_profile: Savory-sweet dashi-soy broth with rich beef and chewy wheat noodles

elevations.title: Build Real Dashi
elevations.instruction: Bring 4 cups water with 4-inch kombu piece to just below boil (never boil kombu). Remove, add packed cup of katsuobushi, steep 5 min, strain. Season with soy, mirin, pinch of sugar.
elevations.why: Real dashi is transcendent. Kombu provides glutamate, bonito provides inosinate - together they create synergistic umami.

elevations.title: Soy-Mirin Glazed Beef
elevations.instruction: Slice beef paper-thin against grain. Sear in batches 30 sec per side. Deglaze with 2 tbsp each soy and mirin. Reduce to glaze (30 sec), toss beef to coat.
elevations.why: Glazing beef separately concentrates savory-sweet flavor on the meat rather than diluting into broth.

elevations.title: Onsen Egg
elevations.instruction: Hold water at 167F for 13 minutes with eggs. Transfer to ice water. Crack over finished udon - white barely set, yolk completely liquid.
elevations.why: At 167F proteins cook differently - custard-like yolk, silky white. Enriches broth when broken.

elevations.title: Toppings Bar
elevations.instruction: Set out shichimi togarashi, torn nori, sliced scallions, and tenkasu (crispy tempura bits) for everyone to customize.
elevations.why: Crunch of tenkasu against soft noodles, heat of shichimi, umami of nori - different experience every bite.

designers_note: Niku udon is Japanese soul food. The secret is the broth. If the broth is right, everything else falls into place. Do not skip real dashi.

name: Mac and Cheese (Elsie Kid Night)
base_description: Classic baked mac and cheese for Thursday kid-friendly dinner with fruit and berries and cream dessert

elevations.title: Three-Cheese Blend
elevations.instruction: Use 50% sharp cheddar, 30% Gruyere, 20% American cheese. The American contains sodium citrate which prevents grainy sauce.
elevations.why: American cheese is an emulsifier in disguise. Cheddar brings sharpness, Gruyere depth, American keeps it silky.

elevations.title: Buttered Panko Crust
elevations.instruction: Toss 1 cup panko with 2 tbsp melted butter, pinch garlic powder, 1 tbsp grated Parm. Spread over mac, bake 375F until deeply golden and shattery.
elevations.why: Panko stays airy and crispy where regular breadcrumbs get dense. Butter browns the crumbs.

elevations.title: Mustard Powder in the Roux
elevations.instruction: Whisk 1 tsp dry mustard powder and pinch cayenne into the flour when making roux. Cook 1 minute before adding milk.
elevations.why: Mustard powder amplifies cheese perception without tasting mustardy. Professional trick.

elevations.title: Undercook Pasta by 3 Minutes
elevations.instruction: Boil macaroni 3 minutes short of package time. It finishes cooking in sauce and oven. Overcooked noodles turn to mush.
elevations.why: Pasta absorbs sauce and continues cooking. If al dente going in, overcooked coming out.

designers_note: Mac and cheese is not a recipe to be clever with. It is a recipe to be precise with. Proper emulsification, right cheese blend, and a non-negotiable crunchy top.

name: Linguini with Clams
base_description: Classic linguini alle vongole - pasta with fresh clams in white wine, garlic, and olive oil
flavor_profile: Briny, garlicky, bright with wine and parsley, clean ocean flavor

elevations.title: Finish Pasta in Clam Broth
elevations.instruction: Steam clams open first, reserve and strain all liquor. Cook linguini 2 min short, finish directly in clam broth with pasta water. Starch-clam liquor creates silky, briny sauce.
elevations.why: Finishing in sauce is the difference between pasta with sauce on top and pasta that IS the sauce.

elevations.title: Garlic Three Ways
elevations.instruction: (1) Thinly sliced garlic cooked golden in olive oil as base. (2) One clove grated raw into sauce at end. (3) Garlic-infused breadcrumbs as finish. Three textures, three intensities.
elevations.why: Cooked garlic is sweet, raw is sharp, breadcrumb garlic is toasty. All three create complete garlic experience.

elevations.title: Pangritata (Crispy Garlic Breadcrumbs)
elevations.instruction: Toast coarse breadcrumbs in olive oil with minced garlic, red pepper flakes, and lemon zest until deeply golden. Scatter over plated pasta.
elevations.why: Italians do not put cheese on seafood pasta. Pangritata provides the same textural satisfaction without dairy.

elevations.title: White Wine Reduction and Lemon Finish
elevations.instruction: Use dry Vermentino or Pinot Grigio, reduce by two-thirds before adding clam broth. Finish with lemon squeeze and rough-chopped parsley.
elevations.why: Properly reduced wine loses alcohol but concentrates fruit and acid. Lemon at the end wakes it all up.

designers_note: One of the simplest and most perfect Italian dishes. Five ingredients, zero margin for error. The clam liquor IS the sauce. No cream. No butter. No cheese. Respect the ocean.

name: Pizza Night (Three Pies)
base_description: Saturday party: Buffalo Chicken White Pie with capers/blue cheese, Classic Cheese and Pepperoni, Mac and Cheese Pizza
flavor_profile: Three profiles: spicy-tangy-creamy, classic savory, rich-cheesy-comfort

elevations.title: 72-Hour Cold Fermented Dough
elevations.instruction: Make dough 3 days ahead. Bread flour, 65% hydration, 1/4 tsp yeast per 500g flour, 3% salt. Refrigerate 72 hours. Pull out 2 hours before baking.
elevations.why: Cold fermentation develops organic acids and alcohols for complex, tangy flavor. Better gluten structure too.

elevations.title: Blue Cheese Bechamel for Buffalo Pie
elevations.instruction: Make light bechamel with butter, flour, milk. Off heat, crumble in Gorgonzola dolce until melted. Spread as base. Top with buffalo chicken, mozz, capers, thin celery slices.
elevations.why: Bechamel distributes funky flavor evenly rather than random clumps. Capers add briny pops, celery adds freshness.

elevations.title: Cup-and-Char Pepperoni
elevations.instruction: Use natural-casing pepperoni sliced thick. The casing causes edges to curl into cups that pool with rendered spicy fat. Place on top of cheese.
elevations.why: Curled edges get crispy, center stays tender. Little pools of spicy fat are concentrated flavor bombs.

elevations.title: Hot Honey Drizzle
elevations.instruction: After pulling pepperoni pie from oven, drizzle with hot honey (3 tbsp honey + 1 tsp red pepper flakes, warmed).
elevations.why: Sweet heat against salty crispy pepperoni is transcendent. One drizzle converts skeptics.

designers_note: Three pies, three chances to show off. Buffalo white pie is the statement, pepperoni with hot honey is the crowd-pleaser, mac and cheese pizza is the conversation starter. Start oven 45 minutes early.
